correctness.rationale: For every ring size n≥3 and every permutation, the deterministic symbolic source map of sequential right-copy updates equals the first strict clockwise cyclic-ascent site. Its image is exactly the 2^k block-constant core, on which sweep rotates k coordinates, and every image word has exactly 2^{n-k} preimages; this proves the full entrance/period/basin claims. Classical Möbius inversion gives each exact primitive-word count, the cyclic-max rooting bijection gives the Eulerian frequency, and a one-dependent CLT with an exponential proper-divisor bound proves the random-scan normal law. A separate exhaustive bitwise functional-graph program checks all orders for n=3..7; a symbolic copy-source verifier checks all orders n=3..8 and divisors through 24. Finite tests supplement the all-n argument.

originality.rationale: The exact Rule 170 all-scan permutation/period/basin classification is not implied by the inspected published asynchronous ECA results or the closest published model results. Macauley–McCammond–Mortveit classify scan-independence of periodic sets, de Oliveira et al. analyze update-synchronism sensitivity and give Rule 170 schedule-map distinctions, and Donoso-Leiva et al. exhibit a consensus-inducing scan. value.rationale: Ordered asynchronous copying is a natural baseline of scan-order sensitivity, making exact effects of scheduling a motivated dynamical question. Rather than only observing a fixed scan or maximizing one period, this determines the complete recurrent core, all necklace orbit populations, individual basin sizes, precise Eulerian frequencies of different global maps and a nondegenerate Gaussian temporal-clock law under random schedules. The uniform-basin property distinguishes this collapse from run-dependent binary necklace systems; it can serve as a sharp benchmark for more elaborate asynchronous local rules. The class is infinite in both ring size and schedule and is not an arbitrary isolated finite computation.
